issue_context.title: service with Type=exec startup race condition
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

252

### Used distribution

CentOS Stream 9

### Linux kernel version used

5.12

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

When starting a transient service  with `Type=exec`, if  `execve()` succeeds,  resulting systemd `Job` should complete with `result=done` and systemd `Service` should  reach `running` state.
Example:
```
$ systemd-run -p Type=exec  --wait /bin/bash -c 'exit 1'
Running as unit: run-u484.service
Finished with result: exit-code
Main processes terminated with: code=exited/status=1
Service runtime: 6ms
CPU time consumed: 5ms
IO bytes read: 0B
IO bytes written: 0B
```

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

When command in `ExecStart=` exits immediately, resulting systemd `Job` **can**  fail with `result=failed` and systemd `Service` might skip `running` state
```
$ systemd-run -p Type=exec  --wait /bin/bash -c 'exit 1'
Job for run-u465.service failed because the control process exited with error code.
See "systemctl status run-u465.service" and "journalctl -xeu run-u465.service" for details.
```

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Launch multiple services concurrently:
```
$ seq 10 | parallel -k "echo =={}; sudo systemd-run -p Type=exec  --wait /bin/bash -c 'exit 1'"
```

comments:
Thanks for the report.
That looks like a race between SIGCHLD and read from exec_fd.
There is [reasoning](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/1108285baa231929e9521309baf12470f763c76a/src/core/service.c#L1525) for the priorities, however, we'd still need to distinguish SIGCHLD before and after execve(2). That could be achived by checking `servcice->exec_fd_hot` when handling SIGCHLD.
@Werkov 

Thanks!

> That looks like a race between SIGCHLD and read from exec_fd.
There is [reasoning](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/1108285baa231929e9521309baf12470f763c76a/src/core/service.c#L1525) for the priorities

It seems SIGCHLD has higher priority (smaller number) than exec_fd? 
```
# sigchild
sd_event_source_set_priority(m->sigchld_event_source, SD_EVENT_PRIORITY_NORMAL-7);
...
# exec_fd
sd_event_source_set_priority(source, SD_EVENT_PRIORITY_NORMAL-3);
```
I guess this explains it: when process exits quickly, both exec_fd and SIGCHLD are ready but systemd ends up processing SIGCHILD first. 

I think giving exec_fd higher priority would completely fix the problem (assuming event ordering is always propagated correctly from the kernel).

> That could be achived by checking servcice->exec_fd_hot when handling SIGCHLD.

AFAIK It is still possible to get SIGCHLD before the first read from `exec_fd` i.e. when `exec_fd_hot` = false.

review_comments: please explain the race briefly here. i.e. something like "This is a bit higher priority than SIGCHLD to make sure we do not mistake a process starting successfully and quickly failing after that with a process failing to start."
hmm, NORMAL-8 would put this at the same level as the sd_notify() messages, which I think we should be careful with. i.e. we want this to be handled before sd_notify() generally.
